correctness.rationale: For each fixed connected graph the rates on a proper nonempty set S are |S| downward and λc(S) upward, where c(S)≥1. The first loss has mean wait 1/n and a uniformly chosen vertex. A monotone successful excursion gives Z/(nλ^(n−1)) at leading order. With u up jumps a successful excursion needs n−1+u specified down jumps after that first loss. At most n^(n−1+2u) state paths have this length for each initial state and each specified down step costs at most λ^−1. Summing the geometric bound at λ>n² bounds the nonmonotone contribution by O_G(λ^−n). In blocks of at most n−1 jumps there is probability uniformly bounded below of ending an excursion by consecutive up moves to full occupancy, and proper-state holding times have mean at most 1/λ. The mean excursion is O_G(1/λ). Renewal gives the mean trial time divided by success probability even if duration and success are dependent. The anchored order-chamber gaps have unit Jacobian, and every edge contributes its intervening gaps, yielding exactly the inverse cuts. Tree differences give independent one-edge integrals of 2. For unicyclic graphs use an anchor on the cycle (the formula was proved for every anchor), integrate the n−ell off-cycle edges, and reduce to the ell-fold convolution of exp(−|x|) at zero. Fourier inversion gives 2^ell times the zero density of an ell-fold normalized Laplace sum, namely binom(2ell−2,ell−1)/2^(ell−1) for the cycle integral. The successive multiplier ratio is 2ell/(2ell−1). The normalization is fixed graph, fully occupied start and unit loss, not a joint size-rate limit.
correctness.replay: From /workspace run python3 branches/independent_reproduction.py 5. Direct rational permutation sums matched the formulas for all 145 labeled trees and 238 labeled unicyclic graphs through five vertices. The source verifier was read, not run. Independent two-vertex birth-death equations give E[T]=(λ+3)/2, agreeing with the n=2 coefficient. These checks do not prove the infinite-rate theorem; the excursion proof does.

evidence: In equation (7) of 2d2ad5c19a59, combine opposite unit arcs and anchor a cycle vertex. An off-cycle leaf integral is 2 independently of its parent. Repeat until the cycle remains. Edge differences make the final edge displacement the negative sum of the others, so the remaining integral is the ell-fold convolution of exp(−|x|) at zero.

Its Fourier transform is 2/(1+t²), yielding the central binomial coefficient divided by 2^(ell−1) via the beta integral. Ratios of successive binomial coefficients yield the frozen monotonicity statement.

originality.rationale: The configured 2d2ad5c19a59 theorem expressly covers the leading permutation coefficient, the integral and the tree law, with directed/weighted generality. On both-way unit edges they are the frozen results. The additional unicyclic formula, while not printed there, follows mechanically from that same known integral by removing leaves and a standard one-dimensional Laplace convolution. 9facf36b623e separately gives exactly the fixed-graph leading mean law. Thus coverage is substantive, not just use of the same terminology. Neither catalogue path date is used to infer historical precedence or provenance.
